entry.name: dac~
entry.description: The dac~ ("digital-to-analog converter") object sends its signal inputs to audio hardware. Double-click on a dac~ to open the Audio Status window to configure audio settings and hardware.

arguments.name: outputs
arguments.description: You can create aobject with one or more logical channel numbers between 1 and 1024. Logical channels are assigned to audio device channels using either the Audio Status window, its I/O Mappings subwindow, or anobject (with keyword). If the computer's built-in audio hardware is being used, there will be two output channels available. Other audio drivers and/or devices may have more than two channels. If no argument is typed in,will have two inlets, for input channels 1 and 2.If a symbol is provided as the first argument to aobject, its output will be sent to the Max mixer. Ifinstances in a patcher hierarchy share the same name they will use the same mixer output.

messages.name: int
messages.description: A non-zero number turns on audio processing in all loaded patches.turns off audio processing in all loaded patches.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Set the logical output channels for each signal inlet
messages.description: comprised of integers sets the logical output channels for each signal inlet in order from left to right.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Set the output channel for signal inlet where themessage was received
messages.description: In any inlet: The word, followed by a number, sets the logical output channel for the signal inlet in which themessage was received. For instance, sendingto the left inlet ofmakes the signal coming in the left inlet output to logical output channel 3.Note that if the audio is on and you use themessage to change ato use logical channels that are not currently in use, no sound will be heard from these channels until the audio is turned off and on again. For example, if you have aobject with arguments 1 2 3 4 and signals are only connected to the two leftmost inlets (for channels 1 and 2), the messagewill not immediately route the leftmost audio signal to logical channel 3, because it is not currently in use. A method to get around this is to connect ato each channel of ayou plan on using for amessage. At this point, you might as well use aorobject to do something similar before the audio signal reaches the.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: A signal coming into an inlet ofis sent to the audio output channel corresponding to the inlet. The signal must be between -1 and 1 to avoid clipping.

messages.name: start
messages.digest: Turn on audio processing in all loaded patches.
messages.description: Turns on audio processing in all loaded patches.

messages.name: startwindow
messages.digest: Enable audio processing in local patch and subpatches only
messages.description: Turns on audio processing only in the patch in which thisis located, and in subpatches of that patch. Turns off audio processing in all other patches.

messages.name: stop
messages.digest: Disable audio processing in all loaded patches
messages.description: Turns off audio processing in all loaded patches.

messages.name: wclose
messages.description: Closes the Audio Status window if it is open.
